# Create and advance a character

**REVIEWED CHARACTER FOUNDATION — authored operational PLAYTEST candidate.** The [source conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_CONFERENCE.md) and [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_EXACT_REVIEW.md), with both requested wording repairs applied, settle the class foundations and advancement rules below. Use the [17-class tables](CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_TABLES.md) beside this guide. Use the later reviewed ancestry/background and equipment guides for their stated scopes, and the reviewed language chapter for language grants and records. Remaining option dependencies and live companion parity are still separate work.

## Begin a character sheet

1. **Record the concept and first Base class.** Choose one of the 17 classes. Start at character level 1 and that class’s level 1. Keep a chronological level record and the order in which you enter classes. Arch and Hero are later stages within a class, not additional Base classes. The former Fighter/Swashbuckler entries and separate historical prestige records supply no extra starting class or automatic grants.
2. **Generate six abilities.** Choose the method before generating scores: roll four d6, discard the lowest and total the other three, six times; or assign the standard array 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8. Assign those six results once to STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS and CHA. Keep the original rolls. Do not reroll, mix methods or select a preferred set without a separate table rule. The optional provisional point-buy method below is also available.
3. **Record ancestry and any required variant.** Apply its actual ability increases once after assigning scores, resolving an OR choice once. Record size, movement, senses, languages and each complete trait procedure from its source. Trait names alone are insufficient. Do not stack alternative builder/racial-variant entries onto the same book trait. Use the reviewed ancestry/background integration and complete source bindings for all14 base ancestries and45 variants; apply the reviewed language chapter to their actual language grants. This step grants no authority to revise their cosmology or origin lore.
4. **Choose one background.** Record its actual skills, tools, languages, feature and starting package, including required choices. Use the reviewed ancestry/background guide and complete source bindings for the20 background packages; its named outstanding interfaces remain outstanding. The source permits a custom background with two skills, two tools/languages, equipment and a Reputation-related feature developed with the Director; that permission does not supply an invented unlimited feature or a second background.
5. **Apply starting training.** Use this first class’s saves, armor, weapons, tools and number of skill choices from the foundation tables. Use the class list for each skill choice. Add ancestry/background training with the duplicate procedure below. Proficiency grants training, not equipment ownership, spells or a second PB on one roll.
6. **Set HP, Hit Dice and proficiency.** First-character-level base HP is the maximum face of this class’s HD; add current CON modifier, minimum 1. Record one unspent Hit Die of that size. At level 1 PB is +2. Keep base maximum HP separate from later effects, reductions and systemic multipliers.
7. **Acquire the actual class kit.** Follow the class’s own level-1 engine, automatic grants and scheduled choices. Ordinary classes start with four Base choices, at least two active, where their schedule says so. Druid, Oracle and Paladin have explicit schedules; follow those instead. Make required engine/path choices, such as Oracle Mystery and Curse, exactly when their cards require them. Use the [class library](CLASS_PLAYTEST_INDEX.md), [legal acquisition examples](CLASS_PLAYTEST_BUILD_EXAMPLES.md), and [Paladin oath pairs](PALADIN_OATHS_AND_OATHBREAKERS.md). No legacy Skill Points, companion feature strings or historical prestige rows add grants to this schedule.
8. **Record magic and class resources.** Use the class’s current Core V2 RP table and rank gates, plus its actual known/prepared/spellbook procedure. Record each selected operational spell’s identity and casting class. Enough RP never unlocks a rank or school. Oracle uses Revelation Charges; Soldier and Warrior have no general RP casting. Initial class resources and empty stores follow their actual engine setup; preparation or copying is not waived. Read [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md) and [spell integration](SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md).
9. **Choose starting equipment or money.** Take the class and background packages, **or** roll the first class’s starting wealth and buy equipment with it. Wealth replaces all starting package equipment, including package money; background training and features remain. Record purchases, remaining coins, ammunition, components, containers, quantities and actual weight/Load. An item must exist with usable statistics; a proficiency or feature label cannot create it. Use the reviewed equipment/acquisition guide, complete item procedures and starting-package records; keep any actually unresolved entry visible.
10. **Finish the derived sheet.** Calculate ability modifiers, trained saves and skills, legal equipped AC, movement, weapon attacks, class attacks/DCs and actual resource caps. Choose one applicable AC formula rather than adding formulas. A normal proficient attack is d20 + PB + its actual attack modifier; class DC is 8 + PB + its actual class modifier. Use actual negative modifiers; the class card’s minimum-1 effect modifier is not a minimum attack/DC modifier. Note conditions, Wounds, supplies and other scene state separately. Record the source/card for every nonordinary number.

An ancestry/background feature, spell or item that remains mechanically unresolved is a visible unfinished dependency. A checked box or a saved companion character does not resolve that dependency.

## Abilities and training

Ability modifier = floor((score − 10) / 2), including negative results. For example, 8 gives −1, 13 gives +1 and 16 gives +3.

**Optional new candidate method:** 27-point buy, scores 8–15 before ancestry. Costs are 8:0, 9:1, 10:2, 11:3, 12:4, 13:5, 14:7, 15:9. Spend no more than 27 points across six scores; no score outside that range. This adopts the existing companion method as a provisional option, not a claim that the book already specified it.

Resolve duplicate training as follows:

- For a selectable grant, choose another eligible option from that grant’s own list.
- For a fixed ancestry/background skill grant with no alternative list, choose another of the 20 basic skills.
- For a duplicated tool, choose another eligible tool from that grant’s list; if it has no list, use another actually supported tool in the same broad category.
- Duplicate armor, weapon, save or multiclass chassis training gives no skill or feat compensation. A new multiclass skill selection must still use its own permitted list.
- Duplicate proficiency never creates Expertise unless an exact feature says so. If a proficiency grant requires a choice and every legal option for that grant is already possessed, that grant provides no additional proficiency. Character creation, multiclass entry or advancement remains legal. Do not substitute a feat, Expertise, another category of proficiency, an unrelated skill/tool, or a banked future selection. This applies to skill and tool lists, including a legal replacement list or category that is itself exhausted.

PB is applied once to a check even if a skill and tool both qualify. An exact Expertise multiplier modifies that one proficiency contribution; it does not add another independent PB.

## Gain a level

Opening campaigns officially use milestones. The Director’s announced milestones grant advancement; a CR-to-XP UI helper is not the official Opening reward law. The book’s cumulative XP thresholds remain available for tables using optional XP. See [XP provenance](XP_ADVANCEMENT_CANON.md).

Each earned advancement adds one total character level, to a combined maximum of 20. Choose one existing Base class to advance, or enter one new Base class if eligible. Process multiple earned levels one at a time; do not skip intervening choices.

1. Record the gained class and new class level. Recalculate total level and PB: +2 at total 1–4, +3 at 5–8, +4 at 9–12, +5 at 13–16, +6 at 17–20.
2. Add one new unspent Hit Die of the gained class’s size. Previously spent Hit Dice remain spent; gaining this die does not refresh any earlier die. For HP, roll that die or use its fixed rounded-up average: d6→4, d8→5, d10→6, d12→7. Record the base result before CON. This includes taking a new class’s first level after character level 1; maximum first-level HP is never granted again.
3. Apply exactly the gained class’s acquisition row, automatic improvements and class-level prerequisites. Complete its choices and any newly reached Arch/Hero gate. Automatic grants, scheduled selections and ASIs are distinct; do not pay a selection twice or grant an extra selection because the same feature appears in a legacy table.
4. At an ASI milestone, increase one score by 2 or two scores by 1, normally no higher than 20, or select one eligible operational feat. Ordinary milestones are class levels 4/8/12/16/19; Oracle uses 4/8/14/19. Follow any already-reviewed specific exception. No starting feat or repeatable feat is implied. [Eight complete feat options](FEAT_PLAYTEST_INDEX.md) do not make the other 327 complete.
5. Update legal repertoire, prepared capacity, class scaling and resource maxima at the gained **class** level. Use class-specific Druid preparation, Wizard spellbook/matrices and other explicit rules before generic acquisition defaults. New capacity does not provide an unnamed spell, an unearned choice, a filled Echo record or an extra prepared spell without the required preparation procedure.
6. Recompute base maximum HP from all attained-level records using current CON: sum(max(1, each stored base value + current CON modifier)). Then apply the separate [maximum-HP ledger](MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST.md), including compatible bonuses, reductions and systemic factors. Do not feed an already modified maximum back in as the base.
7. Keep current HP and spent resources unchanged except for a downward clamp when a maximum falls. An ordinary level-up is not healing or a rest: it cannot revive a downed/dead character, erase Wounds or refill already spent Hit Dice, RP, RC, class pools, item charges or uses. Newly granted features still follow an explicit acquisition/initialization clause if they have one; “gain a maximum” alone does not mean “restore current.”

**New HP completion:** each level’s HP contribution has a minimum of 1. Recompute those individual floors after permanent CON changes. This preserves retroactive CON adjustment without a naive level×modifier-change formula that can bypass a floor. Capacity increases grant no current HP; decreases can clamp current HP without damage/healing triggers, consistent with the reviewed maximum-HP interface. Temporary ability effects follow their own actual source rules rather than being silently treated as permanent advancement.

No banked card selections, free retraining or free respec is introduced. Use an existing explicit replacement/retraining procedure where one exists.

## Multiclass entry and class features

When entering a new Base class, meet the multiclass score prerequisites for **every held class and the new class**. The foundation tables give the exact source gates; a class’s descriptive primary ability is not a substitute. These requirements are checked on new-class entry. Losing a qualifying score later does not erase earned classes/features, though it can prevent entering another new class. Advancing a class already held is not a new-class entry test.

Only the first character class grants its full starting saves and proficiency package. Each later newly entered class grants its separate multiclass proficiency row once. It grants no second background, starting wealth/equipment or full starting skill count. Its genuine level-1 engine/features and acquisition schedule still apply.

**New chassis clarification:** a level-1 card whose sole function is to restate starting armor/weapon proficiency cannot bypass the multiclass table. Paladin Martial Proficiency therefore supplies no heavy-armor bypass. An independent non-chassis mechanic in a feature remains available on its actual terms.

Use the largest equivalent Extra Attack count, never their sum. Use one applicable AC formula, never their sum. Duplicate historical Channel Divinity labels do not manufacture another use pool. Distinct operational class engines and paid techniques remain distinct and obey their own costs and the shared action limits.

Class level controls rank access, acquisitions, S scaling, Arch/Hero gates and finales. Total character level controls PB and optional XP thresholds. A Bard 5 / Mage 5 is total 10 with PB +4, but neither class has reached its Hero gate.

## One shared RP pool

Calculate each eligible class’s own current candidate RP pool at its own class level. Sort these classes by:

1. Caster tier: Full (Cleric, Druid, Mage, Wizard), then Half (Paladin, Ranger), then Hybrid (Bard, Shaman, Mirrorsage, Crimson Agent), then Minor (Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker).
2. Within a tier, higher class level first.
3. If class levels tie, higher actual RP pool first.
4. If both tie, the class acquired earlier first. Record that order; do not choose a different primary per cast.

Oracle, Soldier and Warrior contribute no RP pool. Maximum RP = the first class’s full pool + ceil(one quarter of the second class’s pool). With only one eligible class use its pool; with none, maximum RP is 0. Third and later eligible classes contribute no extra capacity, while retaining their earned class features and legal repertoire. Use current Core V2 candidate pools, not the older smaller companion-derived tables.

All RP-paid spells and techniques use this one merged pool unless an exact rule names another resource. RC, BG, Momentum, Ki, Conviction, Lay on Hands and other class resources remain separate. A change in the primary class or maximum is not recovery: preserve current RP and clamp only if above the new maximum. This can reduce maximum RP when a newly entered higher-tier class becomes primary; do not silently choose a larger lower-tier pool instead.

Each ordinary cast declares its casting class before costs. That class must independently know/prepare the spell, meet its school/rank gate and supply its own casting ability. Another class’s levels or repertoire cannot fill those requirements. Where two classes know the same spell, choosing its casting class does not create a second spell identity.

## Shared strain, recovery and concentration

Keep one character-wide Dissonance number and one Refrain history across classes. For a cast, evaluate limit = max(4, 2 + total-character PB + max(0, the actual casting-class modifier)). Apply the existing surcharges, ranked-cast cutoff, repetition and explicit class exceptions from [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md). Switching casting class does not clear either history; the same spell identity still repeats. Class cadence benefits require their actual ownership and trigger conditions. Idle decay and Grounding occur once per character turn, not once per class.

Generic Retune happens once per eligible completed short rest for the character. It restores max(0, round-half-up(maximum RP / 4) + the current primary RP class’s casting modifier), capped at the merged maximum, and clears Dissonance. Optional once/day meditation uses that same primary class’s positive modifier and the existing PB-based strain reduction. Long-rest RP recovery restores the merged pool under the existing recovery rules. None of these generic procedures duplicates because the character has more classes or recovers a different named resource without its own rule.

Oracle Revelations use RC and do not generate ordinary Weave strain unless expressly stated; they do not clear existing strain/Refrain from another class. One ordinary concentration slot is shared across classes, with only the exact already-reviewed linked-effect exceptions such as Spell Tether, Tethered Cast and Crimson Harmony. No generic Overcast option is reintroduced.

## Worked foundation checks

- **First Bard level:** CON 14 gives modifier +2; base HP 8+2 = 10, one d8 Hit Die and PB +2. Choose three class skills from the 20-skill list and four eligible Base cards with at least two active, as the Bard schedule directs. Background/ancestry grants remain separate and must be fully specified before play.
- **Bard 1→2 without a rest:** fixed HP base 5 and CON +2 increase base maximum 10→17. If current HP was 6 it stays 6. The second Bard level grants its actual two Base selections. A higher RP maximum does not refill spent RP.
- **New class does not repeat maximum HP:** a Bard 3 taking Mage 1 adds d6 roll or fixed 4, plus CON; it does not add 6 merely because Mage is class level 1. Total PB is still +2 at character level 4. The character must meet Bard CHA 13 and Mage INT 13 before entry.
- **Retroactive CON with floors:** a d6 first level recorded as 6 and a later d6 roll recorded as 1 give contributions 4 and 1 at CON 6 (−2), total 5. At CON 8 (−1) they give 5 and 1, total 6. Adding a naive two levels × +1 would incorrectly give 7.
- **A three-class caster:** Cleric 6, Druid 6 and Wizard 1 use Cleric/Druid as the two Full-tier contributors because class level precedes pool size. Their own level-6 pools are 15 each, giving 15+ceil(15/4) = 19 RP; earlier acquisition breaks their tie. Wizard 1 adds no RP but retains its own legal Wizard 1 spell access. Total 13 supplies PB +5; no class has a Hero gate.
- **Different casting stats:** at total level 6, PB +3, a modifier +3 caster has limit 8 and a modifier +1 caster has limit 6. Shared Dissonance 6 is below the first limit but at the second. Casting through the second class uses its surcharge; the shared strain number and spell repetition history survive the switch.
- **Monk wealth:** rolling 5d4 for a total of 12 gives 12 gp, not 120 gp. No background-package money is added if this money method replaces the packages.
- **Later Paladin:** a non-Paladin’s entry uses the Paladin multiclass row. Its level-1 Martial Proficiency restatement grants no extra heavy armor or second set of saving-throw proficiencies.

The [reference checks](CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_VALIDATION.json) verify selected calculations and source preservation. They do not execute a live character builder, certify every acquisition interaction or replace human playtesting.

## Source decisions and remaining work

The foundation uses reviewed active class contracts first, then detailed class entries, the Classes Table as fallback and companion data only for actual gaps. The [source evidence](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_SOURCE_EVIDENCE.json) retains every disputed chassis entry, original skill list and source hash. All original books, legacy UI data and class cards remain unchanged.

New candidate decisions are explicitly identified: missing class skill lists, Oracle’s starting Arcana substitution, Tinker’s Engineering option, bounded favored/blade weapon choices, optional point buy, duplicate-grant resolution, per-level HP floors and capacity-only advancement, precise multiclass entry/chassis rules, final RP tie-breaking and shared strain/recovery interpretation. These are authored playtest rules rather than approved-book rewrites.

Next dependencies are the remaining selectable-content and named ancestry/background/equipment interfaces, feat acquisition, remaining spells, the expedition-to-Haven loop and final joint flow review. Broader runtime, balance and publication remain separate. Cosmology stays untouched until after the authorized GitHub push has succeeded and its remote commit is verified.

CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md.completeText: # Conditions — integrated playtest reference **Status:** reviewed and reference-validated within generic Core condition/recovery scope. All28 Core condition identities preserved. New generic procedures are explicit playtest proposals, not edits to approved books or a claim of game-wide balance. [Core resolution and Wounds](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md) · [Recovery and exposure procedures](CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md) · [Custom rider bindings](CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md) · [Development coverage](GAME_DEVELOPMENT_COVERAGE.md) The Core catalog contains all 28 conditions. The older shared class reference listed 15 of them; that was a reference omission, not lost source data. This overlay supplies the complete reference without modifying the books or that preserved class file. ## Shared handling This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications. Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. A generic cure naming a condition clears its source records unless a reviewed procedure specifies one-record scope. Bleeding Medicine and Burning DEX saves use the specific procedures below. Track Charmed, Frightened, Marked and Grappled relationships separately. Exhaustion, Intoxication, Unity and Wounds use their explicit tracks. Immunity to a named condition prevents that condition, including an inherited component, but does not silently grant immunity to every parent condition that can cause it. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration. Advantages and disadvantages never multiply dice: any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to one normal d20 roll, regardless of the number of sources. Automatic failure of a required check/save is resolved without a roll. A condition does not give a save where its source grants none. A critical-if-hit rider never makes a missed attack hit. Automatic failure has no rolled total: use ordinary Failure, not Critical Failure or an invented failure margin, unless the source explicitly supplies one. Generic Core Bleeding and Burning join family.bleeding and family.ongoing-fire respectively, with source-owner stack groups. At one identical target timing marker, all due generic and custom groups in that family compete: highest expected unmitigated damage, then earliest application. Only the winning group's source-permitted instances deal damage. All due groups consume that tick; losers do not defer or bank it. Different printed markers resolve separately. No record also receives a duplicate generic tick. Core generic timing is end of regular target turn; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative preserve one periodic step per complete six seconds with no duplicate interval across initiative transitions. Strain is not globally unique: expedition.strain and warrior.serum-strain are separate source-qualified tracks, both distinct from the six-level Exhaustion condition. See the Strain namespace reference for the current candidate. Oracle one-turn Revelation backlash is also separate from global Exhaustion; its printed penalties and endpoint remain unchanged. Wound Eater feeding failures explicitly use global Exhaustion. Never silently convert similarly named tracks. See CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md for finite recovery, cleansing, substance, Intoxication and Unity procedures. These new proposals are labeled separately from recovered source rules. Conditions do not reveal Director secrets or force player beliefs or decisions. SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. ## Quick index | Condition | Configuration | |---|---| | [Addicted](#addicted) | active provisional overlay | | [Bleeding](#bleeding) | active provisional overlay | | [Blinded](#blinded) | active provisional overlay | | [Burning](#burning) | active provisional overlay | | [Charmed](#charmed) | active provisional overlay | | [Corrupted](#corrupted) | active provisional overlay | | [Dazed](#dazed) | active provisional overlay | | [Deafened](#deafened) | active provisional overlay | | [Exhausted](#exhausted) | active provisional overlay | | [Frightened](#frightened) | active provisional overlay | | [Grappled](#grappled) | active provisional overlay | | [Incapacitated](#incapacitated) | active provisional overlay | | [Intoxicated](#intoxicated) | active provisional overlay | | [Invisible](#invisible) | active provisional overlay | | [Marked](#marked) | active provisional overlay | | [Paralyzed](#paralyzed) | active provisional overlay | | [Petrified](#petrified) | active provisional overlay | | [Poisoned](#poisoned) | active provisional overlay | | [Prone](#prone) | active provisional overlay | | [Resonance Burn](#resonance-burn) | preserved; inactive in this Dissonance configuration | | [Restrained](#restrained) | active provisional overlay | | [Silenced](#silenced) | active provisional overlay | | [Staggered](#staggered) | active provisional overlay | | [Stunned](#stunned) | active provisional overlay | | [Unconscious](#unconscious) | active provisional overlay | | [Unity Exposure](#unity-exposure) | active provisional overlay | | [Withdrawal](#withdrawal) | active provisional overlay | | [Wounded](#wounded) | active provisional overlay | ## Addicted **Preserved Core text:** The creature has dependence on a named substance. Without a maintenance dose after a long rest, it gains Withdrawal. **Effect:** Record dependence on one named substance. After each completed long rest, if the creature has not taken the required maintenance dose for that substance, apply Withdrawal for that substance. Magic that only removes symptoms does not automatically remove dependence, consistent with the source treatment text. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: maintenance dose may relieve that substance's current Withdrawal symptoms without removing Addicted; exact dependence cure procedure remains deferred. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Audit individual substance cards, dose escalation wording, equipment availability and specific cure effects during item integration. Record DC (or 10), magnitude, type and endpoint. **Duration and ending:** Persists until its source or applicable cure ends it. A feature explicitly allowing sight while Blinded overrides only its printed scope. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot see, automatically fails sight-required checks, own attacks have disadvantage, attacks against have advantage. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Full special-senses and vision interaction belongs to the stealth/vision pass. An action, immersion, or successful Dexterity save ends it. **Effect:** At end of the affected creature's regular turn its generic record offers 1d4 fire damage to unified family arbitration, unless its source specifies another magnitude. Only the winning stack group deals damage. Damage immunity does not by itself remove Burning. **Application:** Applied only by an effect that explicitly inflicts Burning. Full immersion of all burning portions does the same. Explicit protected-source exceptions survive. Success ends only that record. An effect explicitly immune to Burning blocks application. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: 1d4 fire fallback, source DC or 10, damage then free ending save; Action/immersion can end before damage. - NEW: shared periodic timing and strongest-record precedence; adjacent helper and immersion boundaries. - SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Unforeseeable or genuinely unknown collateral harm is not retroactively a willing violation. The charmer has advantage on social ability checks against it. Charmed itself never compels affection, obedience, beliefs, allegiance, affirmative protection or self-harm. **Application:** Each application identifies the charmer/source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration and repeat-save/ending procedure. **Stacking:** A creature may be Charmed by more than one source; each source relation is tracked independently. Advantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Charm immunity prevents application. Forced actions from another effect are not made voluntary merely because the creature is Charmed. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies the creature cannot attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects, and gives the charmer advantage on social interaction checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Agency clarification: Charmed never by itself grants control over beliefs, targets or decisions beyond the explicit harm restriction. - Source-faithful correction reviewed in GPT_CUSTOM_RIDER_SECOND_REVIEW.md: Core's unwilling-to-harm restriction is broader than direct targeting; preserve its area/indirect-harm scope without importing mind control. Saves against spells/abilities from individually recorded Evil creatures have disadvantage; its aura can be detected by effects revealing evil. At each completed long rest make DC 15 WIS save or move one moral step Good to Neutral to Evil, leaving law/chaos unchanged. Already Evil remains Evil. Alignment does not compel conduct, party separation, PvP or automatic oathbreaking. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Corrupted apply it. **Duration and ending:** Persists until an explicit cleansing effect or the eight-hour cleansing project in CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md succeeds. Explicit cleansing or protection may override within scope. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: healing effects restore half normal HP; disadvantage on saves against spells/abilities from evil creatures; faint aura detectable by magic revealing evil; at end of each long rest make DC 15 Wisdom save or alignment shifts one step toward evil. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: round half healing down once; guaranteed death-save/Stable one-HP state recovery is not a healing effect. - Source-grounded: individual recorded alignment or Evil tag only; no ancestry/faction inference, forced behavior or automatic conduct violation. - NEW: generic cleansing project supplies a finite recovery route. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Cross-check separately reviewed corruption-sensitive transformations and specific restoration effects. Do not undo completed events. Forced movement is not voluntary movement and remains possible. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: immediate mid-turn handling, each extra turn gets its own mode, one-Action ceiling, explicit action-contained movement exception. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Interaction with future nonstandard action types if any are introduced. It cannot satisfy a rule that specifically requires hearing another creature's command, warning, chant or audible signal. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Deafened apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end condition. **Stacking:** Multiple applications do not compound. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Deafened does not prevent the creature from speaking or supplying its own verbal components unless another condition such as Silenced applies. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches inability to hear and automatic failure of hearing-required checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Operational clarification: 'verbal coordination may fail' means hearing-dependent coordination requirements fail; no generic roll is added. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Future command/audible-coordination features must state whether hearing is required. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 741, definition paragraph 742; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Exhausted **Preserved Core text:** Use the six-level exhaustion track; effects are cumulative and level 6 is death. **Effect:** Track 0–6 cumulative levels: 1 disadvantage ability checks; 2 half Speed after flat changes; 3 disadvantage attacks and saves; 4 maximum HP max(1,floor(otherwise-applicable maximum/2)); 5 Speed zero; 6 death. **Application:** An effect that grants one or more Exhaustion levels increases the track by that amount, maximum 6, unless it explicitly sets a level instead. **Duration and ending:** Eligible beneficial eight-hour long rest removes one level under CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md, at most one generic removal per 24 hours. Derive level-4 maximum from the otherwise-applicable current maximum, never a previously halved value. Clamp HP down when maximum decreases; raising maximum does not heal. Level-5 zero Speed overrides halving. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An explicit Exhaustion immunity blocks levels. Removing Exhaustion from a dead level-6 creature does not restore life; resurrection is still required. **Compatible V6/source details:** - Level 1: disadvantage on ability checks. - Level 2: Speed halved. - Level 3: disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws. - Level 4: hit point maximum halved. - Level 5: Speed reduced to 0. - Level 6: death. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: maximum-HP floor 1, recomputation/clamping and flat-Speed-before-halving order. - NEW: finite generic long-rest recovery; source-specific removal blocks remain. - Recovered V6: six cumulative level effects. Disadvantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fear immunity blocks application. Passive effects continue unless their own rules require consciousness or another condition disables them. Incapacitated by itself does not reduce Speed or prohibit speech. **Application:** Applied by a condition or effect that explicitly says the creature is Incapacitated. **Duration and ending:** Use the parent condition/effect's duration. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Current shared concentration rules end concentration immediately when the creature becomes Incapacitated. Stacks worsen into Dazed and Unconscious. **Effect:** Use the single 0–5 Intoxication track and procedures in CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md. Level 1 grants one fear-save advantage use per continuous nonzero episode and disadvantage precise-memory checks; level 2 additionally gives disadvantage precise DEX/INT checks; level 3 additionally Dazed and Speed-10; levels 4/5 additionally Unconscious and their poisoning/emergency procedures. **Application:** Explicit Intoxication gains advance the dose-driven track. It adds no dose-driven points. Generic direct applications never create floors 3–5. One fear-save advantage use for the entire episode until level 0, never refreshed by moving between positive levels. Other independent Dazed/Unconscious/Poisoned sources remain after intoxication recovers. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An effect explicitly preventing intoxication blocks track gain. Unconscious at level 4 uses the normal Unconscious condition. **Compatible V6/source details:** - Existing Intoxication Track: 0 Sober; 1 Relaxed with advantage on one fear save and disadvantage on precise memory checks; 2 Intoxicated condition; 3 Dazed and Speed -10 ft; 4 Unconscious for 1d4 hours plus Constitution save against poisoning; 5 medical emergency, gain a Wound or die without treatment at Director discretion. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: cumulative condition thresholds, direct-application floor and continuous-episode fear-save limit. - NEW: finite sobriety, poisoning and medical-emergency procedures; source values/conditions preserved. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Individual brew/substance cards still need their complete dose, access and balance audit. Until an observer knows its location, that observer attacks it with disadvantage and it attacks that observer with advantage. Once location is revealed, these Invisible-specific modifiers end for that observer. Do not re-grant them through V6 generic unseen rules solely because it is still Invisible. A special sense actually seeing it bypasses these modifiers. Knowing location is not seeing; effects requiring sight still need sight. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly granting Invisible applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the granting effect's duration. V6 attacks reveal location upon attacking; resolve the revealing attack first, then observers able to perceive evidence know the location. # Healing, survival and resurrection — playtest interface

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED — selected scope only.** The [final notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) closes147 classified class passages plus6 individually reviewed ordinary spell objects. Those6 spells are now operational playtest drafts; the catalog has78 operational and770 unfinished entries. This is a bounded interface, not DD24 completion:131 additional semantic matches and healing content in other domains still need dispositions. Original cards/books are preserved.

[Exact source procedures](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) · [Latest boundary decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_BOUNDARIES.md) · [Supplement decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_SUPPLEMENT_REVIEW.md) · [Reference checks](HEALING_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) · [Source integrity](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json)

## Distinct life operations

| Operation | Result | Restriction interface |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum-HP prevention | Preserve positiveHP instead of crossing a floor | Not HP gain; cannot create positiveHP from0 |
| Ordinary healing | Increase a living creature's normalHP | Apply modifiers, prohibitions, reserve and Critical ceiling |
| Direct state recovery | Specifically defined dying/Stable/HP recovery | Broad cannot-regain-HP applies; ordinary healing modifiers do not |
| Would-die replacement | Replace a pending death before it becomes final | Exact source eligibility; not a generic damage floor |
| Resurrection | Actually dead willing identity returns at printedHP | Separate life transition; actual corpse/soul blockers apply |
| Companion reconstruction | Restore a device/companion through its own source | No general creature resurrection permission |
| TemporaryHP | Separate nonstacking buffer | Not healing, stabilization or resurrection |

Names never select the operation. Phoenix Rebirth heals a still-living ally at0. Cleric Resurrection returns an actual dead identity. Ritual of Undeath's Ward replaces death; ordinary Death Ward is a positive-to-zero floor. Feign death and spirit manifestations are not death or resurrection.

## Damage quantities and resolution

| Quantity | Definition and use |
|---|---|
| resolvedDamage | After defenses, before tempHP; positive damage event iff greater than0 |
| tempAbsorbed | min(tempHP, resolvedDamage) |
| postTempDamage | resolvedDamage minus tempAbsorbed, uncapped by currentHP; Core Instant Death/Wounds |
| actualHpDamage | NormalHP lost to the packet after true prevention; recovery and state-assignment loss excluded |
| actualDamageDealt | NEW anti-overkill bridge: tempAbsorbed plus actualHpDamage; numeric actual-damage drains/reflections |

Ordinary “damages,” “takes damage” and “damaging hit” predicates use a positive resolved packet. Actual-HP wording (Burning Blood/Rewind Wound) uses actualHpDamage. Numeric actual-damage wording (Sanguine Rite/Echo Leech/Merciful Smite/Wound Eater/Gravebrand) uses actualDamageDealt. Source attack/hit predicates remain distinct.

Example: HP10/temp10 takes5: numeric actual damage5, actualHP damage0, positive packet. HP1 under a floor takes5: numeric0 but positive packet. HP3 takes12: numeric3, raw post-temp12. HP0 takes1: numeric0, positive packet and normal death-failure consequences.

Divine Judgment consumes its once-this-actual-target-turn entitlement on a positive packet, then reflects min(Cleric level, max(1, floor(actualDamageDealt/2))). Thus HP1-floor/numeric0 reflects1 and consumes; fully prevented resolved0 does neither. Wrathful Brand/Balanced Scales use the positive predicate where their source says damage occurred.

Resolve a damage event in this order:

1. Snapshot pre-event HP/tempHP/Wounds; resolve defenses, temp absorption and uncapped post-temp damage.
2. Core Instant Death uses postTempDamage minus preHP greater than or equal to effective maximum when reduced to0. It precedes ordinary floors. Open a legal would-die replacement; stop that packet's death procedure. No Wound save or zero-HP failure follows this branch.
3. If not Instant Death, resolve applicable true floors. They cannot raise an already0 creature. They preserve raw damage and attached conditions; a prevented drop creates no drop-only Wound trigger, but half-max/Maiming still applies.
4. Spiral-TouchedIII alone has a specific pre-Wound recovery exception. If positive-to-zero remains, spend its use, preserve that raw crossing trigger, attempt quarter-max direct recovery and apply phase-out. Broad HP-gain prohibition blocks the recovery but not the use/phase.
5. Resolve the one Core Wound save using original post-temp damage and pre-event Wounds. Fatal Wound death opens its own legal replacement window. Actual death ends Spiral phase; a successful independent Ward prevents actual death.
6. Resolve already-zero damage failures/death and its legal replacement window. A successful replacement stops skipped same-packet death branches; never replay a Wound/failure branch merely because replacement changedHP.
7. Finalize a newly surviving0 creature's dying/Stable/knockout state. Only an explicitly triggered post-zero Reaction such as Grace Reversal can act before ordinary zeroHP Reaction loss finalizes.
8. Resolve eligible post-zero Phoenix/Unyielding-style healing only if target still lives, followed by later triggers. This healing never retroactively reduces the triggering packet's numeric damage.

The affected creature chooses among simultaneously eligible offered survival effects, then rechecks remaining triggers. A paid Reaction spends its declared cost; a limited automatic survival use spends when its actual source resolves. A true floor preventing the crossing means Spiral's use is not spent. No generic extra Reaction or return from death is created.

For Ritual Ward, sufficient body and no explicitly unpreventable death are prerequisites. It can intercept Instant Death, fatal Wounds, third death-save failure, eligible direct death and lethal tracks. Positive pre-eventHP→1 is loss prevention and works through Decay. Already0 with HP gain prohibited instead becomes living Stable0: clear counters and establish a d4-hour recovery deadline immediately.

Freeze packetHpLossBeforeReplacement after true floors but before Ward. Ward metrics are min(packetHpLossBeforeReplacement, max(0, preHP minus replacementHP)); never include loss caused solely by assigning a lowerHP state. HP20 takes10 then fatal Wound/Ward1 means actualHP damage10, not19. HP5 takes100 then Ward1 means actualHP damage4, raw100.

Direct death (e.g. Wound EaterIII) produces no damage or Wound save. Its healing requires actual death; a Ward interception prevents that trigger without refunding the paid activation. False LifeI has only its printed floor and failed-death-save replacement modes sharing1/LR; it is not an all-causes Ward.

## ZeroHP permissions and start timing

A conscious but dying creature still rolls at each regular start unless Stable. Extra turns do not advance these regular-start deadlines. Further damage and actual death retain normal consequences.

Mage Undying Spellform partially overrides only zeroHP Unconscious/Incapacitated restrictions: normal speech, voluntary half-Speed movement, normal Action, legal spellcasting with that Action, and starting/maintaining concentration. No independent BA/Reaction. Existing concentration avoids automatic loss from zeroHP, but the triggering damage still requires its concentration save. Separate Stunned/Unconscious/Expedition5 or6/Silence and other restrictions still apply. Healing above0 ends the feature. Expiry at0 destabilizes, cancels the Stable recovery deadline and adds one failure; the third kills normally and permits only an eligible would-die replacement.

Oracle False LifeIII permits exactly one choice during the allowed zeroHP turn: move up to Speed, speak, or activate one Revelation. The latter uses its printed Action/BA/trigger (trigger must occur on that turn), costs and components. It can start concentration; the feature did not preserve earlier concentration. No independent actions accompany the choice.

False LifeV quarter-max direct recovery resolves at its next regular start before the death save. Blocked recovery leaves0 without invented stability; dead creatures do not revive. Spiral phase expires at its next regular start before normal start processing. Fate-BoundIV rerolls a failed death save before committing natural1/counters; use the new result. Its generic death-effect save bonus is not an ordinary death-save modifier. A natural20 whose1HP is blocked uses the previously reviewed Decay bridge: Stable0, cleared counters, immediate d4-hour deadline and preserved used-turn marker. It does not spend Ward. This differs from blocked False LifeV, which remains dying.

## Ordinary healing arithmetic

Determine legal source, recipients, costs, clocks and available entitlements before arithmetic. The helper receives already eligible modifiers; it does not acquire class powers or validate every source for its caller.

Pre-resolution modifiers include Words of Equilibrium's formula M, Zealot's Fervor +S, Throne's Grace +1/die capped S+M, Benevolent Spirits' eligible paid-technique +M, Life Prophecy maximizing dice, and Crane's applicable +S. First compute without conditional add-ons. Only if this preview actually restores at least1HP, recompute that same event once with its eligible add-ons. The preview changes no pools/uses. Base5 minus5 plus a conditional3 remains0; eligible pre-resolution Benevolent3 yields3. Multiple flat class bonuses use the strongest across both passes unless an explicit source exception allows stacking. Rolled extra dice/per-die changes are separate.

Within each permitted reduction plan: formula/bonuses; per-die adjustments; compatible exact fractional multipliers with one floor after multiplication; compatible flat reductions; floor at0; broad HP prohibition; maximum/Critical/reserve caps. Intrinsic Wound Eater and systemic Corrupted remain independent factors. Duplicate same-stat per-die penalties use the strongest. Dice remain dice when maximized/shared; flat Lay on Hands and stored numeric Echoes have zero healing dice.

Blight Totem cannot compound other local healing reducers. Compare systemic factors plus Totem-half alone against systemic factors plus all otherwise compatible local reducers; use the lower result. Compatible halves multiply, compatible distinct flat penalties add, duplicate same-profile groups use strongest. Suppressed reducers do not participate.

Every present, operative, applicable next-positive-healing reduction consumes exactly once when the final event commits if its pre-reduction HP potential was positive. This includes reducers whose arithmetic branch lost to Totem or whose actual gain was later blocked. Zero potential and suppressed records consume none. Two-pass preview never consumes twice.

Critical at3Wounds caps ordinary healing at max(1, effective maximum minus1); it is not a maximumHP reduction and healing cannot lower currentHP. Reserve spends only actualHP restored. A final heal8 with room3 spends3 reserve; blocked healing spends0, other activation costs remain paid. Revival/form changes/encounter starts do not replenish reserve.

## Recovery gates, triggers and loops

False Life curse gates another creature's healing SPELL: optional Insight vs RevelationDC; success permits; failed or declined check rolls d2,1 blocks HP and2 permits. Nonspell recovery and independent nonHP components remain distinct. Burning Blood blocks the cold-tagged HP-healing component only, not independent tempHP/stabilization/resurrection.

Actual positiveHP restoration is required for Radiance's cure, Renewal's Stamina, Sanctified Reprisal and Life Prophecy's RC trigger. Meditative Healing's laterKi and Transcendent Meditation's second-pulseKi are independent components and still resolve when healing caps/blocks. Blood Tithe uses its actual qualifying hostile Bleed-death trigger and finite use; not staged farming.

Passive regeneration includes Bloodthick Node, Rapid Coagulation, Regenerative Mutation and Bio-Stabilizer's modification; these retain Reserve. Finite paid/limited pulses such as Aura of Grace, Living Pulse, Renewal Totem, Blood Feast, Exsanguinate, Hemostasis, Transcendent Meditation, Cellular Reconstruction and Adrenal Floodgate are not passive regeneration. Their own Downed/Incapacitated gates remain. A passive-regeneration prohibition is not a universal healing prohibition.

Lay on Hands retains its5×Paladin-level finite pool and ordinary Long Rest refill. Base Action spends at most level on one target; Hero1/LR spends the entire remaining pool across at most3, each allocation at least1. No RP conversion. Verdict Absolute's explicit qualifying brand-kill refill is a source exception. **Remainder-conference amendment — engine[13] cadence reconciliation:** level17 Wave is1/long rest, superseding the preserved Hero card and earlier guide's1/short-rest wording. This follows the explicit engine reconciliation; the old source remains intact. Wider pool/recharge execution still belongs to the resource pass.

Transfusion donor spends K normalHP; recipient ordinary base is K+floor(K/2). Channel Life spends X; baseX. Donor must remain at least1, tempHP cannot pay, loss is not damage and cannot be prevented/redirected/refunded when recipient gets0. Recipient legal bonuses/reductions apply.

Secondary healing retains root ID and visited application IDs in a shared causal ledger, including across sibling branches. Each link/application can fire at most once/root. Numeric add-ons remain the same packet, creating no new root/child. Legal finite primary healing may trigger unrelated eligible effects.

Stronger source flags override generic provenance: Vitality Link's child blocks every further link; Echo Leech blocks secondary healing/resource triggers; Blood Feast blocks damage/resource triggers; Merciful Smite blocks Smite/heal-copy chains; Crown Undying blocks redirection/heal-copy chains; Echoes/Spiral copies retain their explicit exclusions. Source payment and direct/actual-gain predicates still apply before a child exists.

## Excess healing

OrdinaryMissingHP = effective maximum minus currentHP. Genuine excess is max(0, legal post-reduction healing minus OrdinaryMissingHP). Broad HP prohibition makes legal healing and excess0. Critical's ceiling does not redefine missingHP: max20/HP19/Critical/legalheal10 restores0 but has9 genuine excess; the missing1 is not excess. At HP20, legalheal10 has10 excess.

This quantity alone grants no conversion. A legal converter must satisfy its own costs/caps/cadences. One excess point can fund only one conversion. Source-internal Overflowing Light resolves before outside Cosmic Equilibrium uses remaining excess. Channel Life attaches a packet-wide prohibition on ALL excess-to-tempHP conversion, including another owner's feature. It permits an otherwise eligible Cosmic damage conversion.

**NEW agreed source exclusion:** Unpaid passive regeneration bounded by Mutation Recovery Reserve cannot supply excess-healing conversions unless a future source explicitly grants an exception. This covers Bloodthick Node, Rapid Coagulation, Regenerative Mutation and Bio-Stabilizer as a Bloodthick modifier. FullHP/Critical may compute mathematical excess but grants no Cosmic conversion and spends no Reserve. Do not extend this exclusion to otherwise eligible paid/finite healing merely because it restores0HP.

## Actual resurrection and retained consequences

Require an actually dead, willing identity, legal source body/anchor, location, target limit, elapsed window, paid cost and no applicable resurrection/soul blocker. ReturnedHP is a life transition, unaffected by ordinary healing multipliers or generic living HP-gain prohibitions. Explicit corpse-local and identity/soul blockers are different scopes.

Preserve Wounds/Injuries, Corruption, intrinsic Oracle Curse, debt/legal-death/body claims and spent resources. ThreeWounds is Critical, not continuous automatic death. Clear death counters/Stable deadline but preserve used turn markers and persistent histories. No duplicate creature or resource refresh.

| Class source | Exact selected procedure |
|---|---|
| Cleric Resurrection | Touch one eligible allied body, dead≤60seconds;1HP and printed2S+M tempHP1minute;3Conviction+10RP;1/LR |
| Celestial Resurgence | Up to6 eligible allied corpses30ft, dead≤18elapsedseconds;1HP;5Conviction+10RP;1/LR |
| Divine Rebirth | One successful resurrection by your Cleric feature instead max(1,floor(effectiveMax/2))HP plus printedS+M tempHP1minute;1/LR |
| Thousand Petals | At most6total including at most2eligible corpses20ft;5Ki+5RP;1/LR. Living3S d8+M healing, dead1HP. Corpse died strictly after previous source regular end. Printed floor until next source start |
| Grace Reversal | Source Reaction on surviving positive→0;10RP;one other eligible allied corpse in Oath aura since previous source regular end; Paladin stays0 |
| Soulbound Ritual / Snap Rebuild | Companion/device reconstruction via exact token/slot/expiry restrictions; no generic creature revival |

Thousand Petals revival history is campaign-persistent per Monk-owner/target identity; another Monk/source remains independent. Grace Reversal history is per Paladin-owner/target until that Paladin's qualifying Long Rest. Death of either participant resets neither. Living healing does not spend resurrection history.

Elapsed windows are inclusive (exact60seconds qualifies); previous-end windows are strictly after that typed phase20 marker through the current event. Initiative changes do not rewrite history.

## Lethal tracks after return or replacement

Both an actual resurrection and would-die replacement retain lethal tracks. Exhaustion6 becomes protected exhaustion.lethal-collapse: alive, Unconscious, no voluntary act/travel. Its static lethal endpoint is suspended for this protected return, ending once legally below6. A qualifying Long Rest can occur unconscious with another creature's care/food/water, inactive root cause and no recovery blocker.

Expedition6 retains all six provenance-bearing points and enters its existing collapse. Only genuine24hour Haven care or explicit eligible treatment can reduce it; point removal gates persist. A later positive unprevented gain at6 reevaluates either track's lethal endpoint. A fresh independently legal finite Ward may intervene; collapse is not continuing immunity.

## Removing suppressed Bleed and fire

Cures examine present, unexpired, not-ended records, including temporary suppression/acquired immunity. Initial immunity that prevented application leaves nothing to cure. Damage arbitration and active hooks still exclude suppressed/immune records.

Medicine selects one present eligible Bleed before rolling its printed/source/fallbackDC. A legal positive-potential magical heal invokes every present applicable Bleed endpoint; each Blood Curse instead receives its printedCON save. An actualHP-gain prerequisite still controls a source that expressly requires it.

A legal extinguish Action/full immersion ends all present ordinary-extinguishable fires within its scope; protected/special prerequisite fires persist. A permitted per-record fire DEX ending save remains available while suppressed when a future tick remains; no extra save after the final consumed tick. Cured records never resume when suppression ends.

## Six ordinary spells — reviewed operational playtest drafts

All retain preserved Action/RP/rank/class gates, and range120ft except Ward60ft. V/S/F uses the established M/F focus alternative; no imported material cost.

| Spell | Proposed individual operation |
|---|---|
| Stitch Fate | Rank8/21RP. Living dying0, not Stable/dead. Remove one recorded failure, or direct1HP recovery/clear counters; blocked latter becomes Stable0 with immediate d4-hour deadline. Not retrospective death undo |
| Death Ward | Rank4/7RP, concentration1minute. One positive-to-zero floor at1, then ends. No Instant Death/fatalWound/thirdfailure/lethal-track protection and no already0 recovery |
| Resurrection | Rank7/17RP. One willing identity, sufficient in-range remains, death≤8elapsedhours; return1HP and retained consequences/collapse |
| Mass Resurrection Denial | Rank8/21RP. Fixed20ft-radius sphere, concentration1minute (NEW supersedes Instantaneous). Corpse-local anchor block while remains inside; movement out/conc end/eligible rank8 removal ends block. Bodyless legal formation is not automatically blocked |
| True Resurrection | Rank9/26RP. One actually dead willing known identity, death≤7elapsed days. Usable in-range body or perceived legal unoccupied formation space120ft. Return1HP; every other remains anchor loses eligibility to duplicate that identity. No true-name or guessed soul-plane knowledge requirement |
| Soul Bind | Rank9/26RP, no concentration. Living dying0 perceived targetCHA save; failed save pending60seconds. PositiveHP/Stable ends pending. Death strictly before expiry creates bound identity for24hours from death. Exact expiry wins. One family record per identity; second legal failed save refreshes pending deadline, no post-death recast. Caster death/incapacity does not end it |

Soul Bind removal targets pending creature or existing post-death remains as local anchor. With no remains, removal must expressly free the bound identity/soul; invent no physical anchor. No mind control, ownership or indefinite prison. True Resurrection still obeys actual identity/soul barriers, and an already-living identity is ineligible. Complete objects retain countering, Dissonance/Refrain, costs and source access.

## Temporal dependency and validation boundary

Spiral-TouchedV Time Loop is temporal restoration, not generic resurrection. Its discussed participant contract restores recorded position, life/death/HP/temp/counters, Wounds/linked Injuries, Core/custom conditions, RC, per-encounter uses and snapshot Soul Bind state. Post-snapshot death/body destruction is conceptually undone; already-dead-at-snapshot remains dead. Generic corpse-resurrection denial does not automatically block it.

It does not restore RP/Ki/Conviction/BG, device resources, Mutation Reserve, daily/rest uses, physical consumables or its own spent use. The helper tests that field distinction only. Full equipment/environment topology, corpse/body-part duplication and clock rebasing remain in the dedicated temporal package; Time Loop is not declared fully operational by these tests.

Current selected checks:164 healing/death plus120 unchanged Core damage states;150 control including2 new clarification cases;98 custom including14 cure-presence cases;153 exact source records. These are interface tests, not execution of147 complete class cards, numerical balance, whole-game completion or a substitute for human playtesting.
